doc.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His arm, and Aaron Graves who commuted from Washington
summary: Banter about Harris's arm, then he tells how Graves commuted from Washington to the Jazz Culture Theatre.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Tape changes, reel headers and session breaks

blocks.x: Yeah, I’m wondering how your arm is doing?
[laughs] My arm is doing pretty good today, the bubble on my elbow has left, is leaving. So it’s just about gone.
Is that what causes your arm to go up like that and it seem like you had drawn into a fist, is that what causes?
Unless, you thought that was what caused it [laughs]. No, your remark caused it.

Caused that. [laughs] This cat here, I should mention, there was a young pianist who would come to the Jazz Culture Theatre. I didn’t know him, I didn’t know where he came from. One day I found out his name was Aaron Graves and I found out that he was coming from Washington and going back at night. I said, “You mean to say, you come all the way from Washington, DC and been going back every night?” He said, “Yes.” I say, “Well, do not go back like that again.” So from then on he would stay at my house and he might go back in the morning, and he, sometime. But I didn’t just like the idea, I thought it was beautiful for a pianist to do that, you know.
